cause_plain: Passing a bytes URL to the URL converter without naming a character set crashes. The code tries to decode the bytes using "no encoding" instead of a sensible default.
real_cause: iri_to_uri() decoded a bytes argument with charset before the code that defaults charset to 'utf-8' had run, so bytes.decode() received None.

gate_reasons: text to replace is not unique in src/werkzeug/http.py
cause_plain: A request with a malformed Authorization header, such as one with an empty key like `Bearer =abc, x=y`, crashed the server with an error. The header parser assumed every `key=value` item had a non-empty key.
real_cause: parse_dict_header() indexed key[-1] without checking for an empty key, so a parameter like '=foo' with no name raised IndexError.

cause_plain: The program printed "Hello world" while it had no console to print to. This usually happens with a windowed PyInstaller build. Click tried to write to a missing output stream and crashed.
real_cause: When no console streams exist (e.g. pythonw/PyInstaller windowed apps) _default_text_stdout() returns None and echo() wrote to it without a None check.

cause_plain: A command printed text to an output that only accepts raw bytes, and the print crashed. Users saw a TypeError instead of the message. I couldn't see the calling code, so this is my best reading.
real_cause: echo() set out = out or "" before appending the newline, which turned an empty bytes/bytearray message into a str and then wrote that str to the binary stream.

cause_plain: Building the Docker files crashed when the app tried to load its Dockerfile template. Jinja, the template library, looked up the path separator in a place where that value had gone missing in this environment.
real_cause: loaders.py used os.path.sep, which some path modules (posixpath on certain builds) do not define; the fix switches to os.sep.

cause_plain: Loading a saved config file crashed the worker at startup. The model class is rebuilt from a pickle, and with attribute docstrings turned on, Pydantic tries to read the class's source code. A class rebuilt this way has no source file, so it fails.
real_cause: extract_docstrings_from_cls() caught only OSError from inspect.getsourcelines(), but for classes rebuilt by cloudpickle inspect raises TypeError ('is a built-in class').

cause_plain: A remote 'heartbeat' command reached a worker that wasn't set up to send events. The worker has no event sender, so the command crashed with an error instead of replying.
real_cause: The heartbeat (and enable/disable events) remote control commands used state.consumer.event_dispatcher without checking that it is None when events are disabled.

cause_plain: pip crashed with a raw traceback on a requirements line that has two semicolons and a tab in its environment condition. Users should have seen a clear "Invalid requirement" message that names the bad line. The condition was `python_version >= '2.7'; python_version <\t'3.5'`.
real_cause: parse_req_from_line() built Marker(markers_as_string) without catching InvalidMarker, so a malformed marker in a requirements file crashed pip with a raw traceback.

cause_plain: When the Celery worker shut down, it crashed with an EOFError while draining the pool's task queues. A worker process had already closed its end of the pipe, so the read found nothing.
real_cause: AsynPool._help_stuff_finish() kept draining the inqueue of children that had already exited (or died mid-message), so recv() raised EOFError at shutdown.

cause_plain: A scraped page returned data that is not valid UTF-8 text (it was probably Windows-1252 text). The spider tried to read it as JSON and crashed instead of handling the bad data.
real_cause: TextResponse.json() passed the raw body bytes to json.loads(), which only auto-detects UTF-8/16/32, so a body in another encoding (cp1252) raised UnicodeDecodeError instead of using the response encoding.

lookups: search_code {"text":"A Redis SSL connection URL should use the scheme rediss://."}
cause_plain: The worker crashed at startup while printing its banner, because the Redis result backend settings contradict each other. SSL options are set, but the backend URL starts with redis://, not rediss://. The error text doesn't say which setting is the problem.
real_cause: RedisBackend._params_from_url() raised the scheme-mismatch ValueError whenever SSL params were in connparams, including those supplied by redis_backend_use_ssl, instead of only for SSL params in the URL query.

cause_plain: Running the scrapy command failed at startup because the project's settings module, 'tutorial', could not be found. The command was probably run from outside the project folder, or the project folder was not on Python's import path. Users saw a bare traceback instead of an explanation.
real_cause: get_project_settings() skipped init_env() when SCRAPY_SETTINGS_MODULE was already set, so the project directory was never added to sys.path and the settings module could not be imported.

cause_plain: Printing a Markdown table that has a header row but no data rows crashes with a bare AssertionError. The renderer expects a table body, and there isn't one.
real_cause: TableElement.__rich_console__ asserted that the markdown table had a header and a body, which fails for tables with no body rows.

cause_plain: Importing the rich library crashes when the program is started from a folder that has since been deleted. Python can't find the current folder, so the whole app fails to start.
real_cause: rich/__init__.py called os.getcwd() at import time without handling FileNotFoundError, so importing rich from a deleted working directory failed.

cause_plain: Black crashed while formatting a Python file that has a function parameter with a type annotation. It hit a parameter shape it didn't expect and gave up with a bare error instead of formatting the file.
real_cause: LineGenerator.visit_tname asserted that a tname node has exactly three children, which is false for an annotated parameter inside a '# fmt: skip' one-liner under the preview feature.

cause_plain: Reading a multipart upload part in small chunks (for example 4 bytes) crashed. The reader needs to read at least as many bytes as the boundary marker is long, and it rejected smaller requests.
real_cause: BodyPartReader.read_chunk() tested 'if self._length:' so a Content-Length of 0 was treated as unknown length and the part was read from the stream, tripping the chunk-size assertion.

cause_plain: Running Black on a file reached through a symlink that points outside the project folder made it crash with a raw Python error. It should have skipped the file with a message.
real_cause: get_sources() called path.absolute().relative_to(root) directly, which raises ValueError for a file reached through a symlink that points outside the project root.

cause_plain: Defining a schema with a list of dates or times (for example `List(DateTime())`) crashes when the schema is created. The inner date field looks for schema settings, but it is handed the list field instead of the schema.
real_cause: DateTime._bind_to_schema() read schema.opts from its parent, but when used as an inner field of List/Tuple the parent is a field without opts; the fix uses self.root.opts.

cause_plain: When a test failed with an exception group, pytest crashed while building the failure report. It had filtered out every traceback entry and then tried to read the first one from an empty list. The user saw an internal IndexError instead of the real test failure.
real_cause: FormattedExcinfo.repr_excinfo() indexed traceback[0] for an exception group even when every traceback entry had been hidden, so the cut traceback was empty and raised IndexError.

cause_plain: pytest crashed at the end of the run while drawing the progress line in "times" mode. It tried to add up how long each report took, and one kind of report (a collection report) has no duration.
real_cause: _get_progress_information_message() summed r.duration over all not-yet-reported reports, but with console_output_style=times a skipped module leaves a CollectReport, which has no duration.

cause_plain: Building a link fails when a URL value is named "self" (for example url_for('x', self=1)). Python reads that value as the method's own first argument and raises a TypeError instead of making the link.
real_cause: Flask.url_for() declared self as an ordinary parameter, so a URL value named 'self' passed via **values collided with it; the fix makes self positional-only.

cause_plain: A request to a web address with a path that starts with a double slash, such as http://host//v:h, crashed with a raw low-level parsing error. The library sent the path to its connection layer as if it were a host name. It could not read it, so users got an obscure crash instead of a clear "invalid URL" message.
real_cause: HTTPAdapter.request_url() passed a path starting with '//' through unchanged, and urllib3 then parsed '//v:h' as a network location and failed; the fix collapses the leading slashes.

cause_plain: A native-mode template failed while rendering. Something in the template tried to join a list that contained a number as if every item were text. I couldn't find which template or expression does this, so I'm not proposing a fix.
real_cause: BlockReference.__call__/_async_call joined block output with the module-level str concat instead of environment.concat, so NativeEnvironment blocks returning non-strings failed.

cause_plain: When a POST was redirected into a GET, the new request had no body but still said it was sending 5 bytes. The HTTP library refused to send it, and the request failed.
real_cause: RedirectMiddleware.redirect_headers() kept Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding when a redirect switched the method to GET and dropped the body, so h11 saw too little data for the declared length.

cause_plain: The app crashes on startup. The `POST /` route is set to return "204 No Content", but its function has a return type hint, and FastAPI reads that hint as a response body. A 204 reply can't have a body, so FastAPI refuses to load the app.
real_cause: get_typed_annotation() turned the string annotation 'None' (from postponed annotations) into NoneType rather than None, so the route was treated as having a response body and the 204 assertion failed.

cause_plain: Black reformatted a piece of code, and its own safety check found that the result was not valid Python. Black refused to return it. The cause is a bug in Black's formatting logic, not a mistake by the user.
real_cause: left_hand_split() only checked for a missing opening bracket, not for empty tail leaves, so at line length 1 it produced a split that broke the code and failed the equivalence check.

cause_plain: Black crashed while formatting a file. One line contained a multiline (triple-quoted) string, and the check for whether that line fits needed bracket-nesting data. One of the line's tokens never had that data recorded.
real_cause: blib2to3 Leaf declared bracket_depth only as an annotation and neither __init__ nor clone() set it, so leaves created outside the bracket tracker lacked the attribute that is_line_short_enough() reads.

cause_plain: Loading data with `sentinel` set to null was rejected with "Field may not be null." I found no bug in the library code I could see. This is probably marshmallow working as designed, because the field doesn't allow null.
real_cause: fields.Constant set load_default/dump_default after Field.__init__ had already computed allow_none from a missing default, so a None constant was rejected as null on load.

cause_plain: A class that defines `__attrs_pre_init__` with arguments and has keyword-only fields with defaults can't be set up. Python rejects the generated `__init__` code, so the app crashes on import.
real_cause: _attrs_to_init_script() built the __attrs_pre_init__ call from kw_only argument strings that still included '=default', generating invalid code like a=attr_dict['a'].default=a=....

cause_plain: When a task result object is garbage-collected, Celery tries to unsubscribe from its Redis result channel. If the result has no task id, or the interpreter is shutting down, that cleanup crashes with a TypeError. The error is noisy but happens in cleanup, not in the task itself.
real_cause: BaseKeyValueStoreBackend._get_key_for() passed the task id straight to key_t(), so a uuid.UUID task id made the bytes join raise TypeError.
